title: SDK Guides Modularization Proposal and Implementation Checklist
body:
Purpose and context:

This note proposes a modular documentation architecture for Redwood SDK guides and a pragmatic rollout checklist. Goal is to reduce duplication, make onboarding faster, enable targeted maintenance (per-language, per-feature), and improve snippet testability so docs can be a source of truth for SDK behavior.

Why now:
- Growing number of SDKs (py, js, go, java) with overlapping concepts but inconsistent structure.
- Frequent docs drift when APIs change (esp. streaming and function-calling).
- We want snippet-driven CI and a reusable snippet library to support Playground and Quickstart flows.

High-level principles:
- Single source of truth for API reference: auto-generate from typed annotations + curated hand-written examples for common patterns.
- Modular guide sections: tiny, composable pages we can assemble for language-specific quickstarts and feature deep dives.
- Snippet-first: every example must be runnable via CI; failures block release.
- Shippable examples: Quickstarts are minimal, sample apps are separate repos.
- Localization & accessibility considered from the start.

Proposed docs modules (atomic units):
1) Getting Started (language-specific)
   - Purpose: zero-to-first-call in <5 minutes.
   - Minimal steps: install, auth, simple generate/embeddings call, inspect response, link to troubleshooting.
2) Core Concepts
   - Tokens & billing, model variants, streaming vs non-streaming, function/tool calling, KV cache concepts for local dev.
3) Recipes (composable)
   - Short, focused how-tos (e.g., "low-latency chat loop", "embedding search", "batched inference").
4) API Reference (auto-generated):
   - Methods, request/response schemas, parameter semantics, compatibility notes.
5) Advanced Patterns
   - Batching, caching, retry policies, observability hooks, privacy/PII guidance.
6) CLI and Local Dev
   - Local runner, hermetic mode, example traffic harness for offline testing.
7) Samples & Reference Apps (links to repos)
8) Migration Guides
   - Breaking changes, deprecations, pinning version strategies.
9) Troubleshooting & FAQs
10) Release Notes & Changelog (per SDK)

Authoring conventions and file formats:
- Use markdown for modular pages. Keep files under /content/<lang>/<module>.md.
- Avoid long monolithic pages. Target ~300-600 words per module.
- Metadata header (YAML front matter) keys: title, slug, sdk_language, version_added, canonical_id.
- Snippets in each module must use canonical snippet fence with tags (e.g. ```py runable=example-llm-1).

Snippet library and CI:
- Central snippet registry (directory + manifest) with unique ids. Each snippet includes metadata: language, dependencies, env expectations, run_command.
- CI job matrix executes snippet run commands in containers (py, node). Failure marks docs build failing.
- Promote caching of snippet outputs for quick smoke runs.

Auto-generated API reference approach:
- Source from typed docstrings (py: pydoc + Sphinx-autodoc; js/ts: typedoc).
- Post-process to add Redwood-specific notes, SLOs, and per-endpoint cost hints.
- Hook generation into release pipeline; tag docs with SDK version.

Localization strategy:
- Mark modules as translatable. Use a minimal initial scope: Getting Started + Core Concepts + Recipes (top 20 pages).
- Use community/localization partners for initial languages (EN, FR, DE, JP).

Telemetry and observability for docs:
- Track "first-call" success metric: proportion of users who hit quickstart and successfully make an API call within 10 minutes (via anonymous telemetry when customers opt-in to sample snippets in Playground).
- Page-level usage (views, time-on-page), snippet run counts, and snippet failure rates.

Versioning and release model:
- Docs version = SDK release tag (semver). Default to latest for landing pages; provide selector for older minor versions.
- Backport policy for docs: important bug fixes only to last two minor versions.

Implementation checklist (phased):
Phase 0 (1-2 weeks):
- Audit current SDK docs to map pages to proposed modules. (Owner: Maya)
- Define snippet id schema and place small registry under docs/snippets/manifest.yaml.
Phase 1 (3-6 weeks):
- Create skeletal modular site scaffolding (mkdocs/hugo) and migration script.
- Implement snippet CI job that can run 1) python snippets 2) node snippets.
- Convert top 5 "Getting Started" pages into modular format and wire up runnable snippets.
Phase 2 (6-10 weeks):
- Auto-generated API reference pipeline (prototype for Python).
- Wire Playground to use canonical snippets for "Try in Playground".
- Add telemetry hooks for snippet runs and page-level metrics.
Phase 3 (10-16 weeks):
- Migrate remaining SDK guides, add localization pipeline for top pages.
- Create sample-app repository templates and link from docs.
- Document release & backport process for docs.

Rollout plan and risk mitigation:
- Ship iteratively; start with Python and JS SDKs where most users are.
- Keep old monolith docs live behind /legacy/ until parity is reached.
- Early adopter program: invite 5 partner teams to try new quickstarts and provide feedback.

Success metrics:
- Reduction in time-to-first-successful-call (target: 40% drop for new users).
- Snippet failure rate < 2% in CI after stabilization.
- Reduction in docs maintenance PR volume for cross-cutting changes (e.g., auth changes) by 50% because of single-source snippets.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Which static site generator (MkDocs vs Hugo) — preference: MkDocs for python ecosystem but need performance tests for multi-language builds.
- Where to host snippet registry (monorepo docs vs separate snippets service).
- How to handle secrets in runnable examples (use ephemeral tokens + test harness).

Next steps (immediate):
- Quick audit: list of 25 highest-traffic pages. (Action: Maya, due 2025-02-21)
- Spike: CI snippet runner (first-pass) for python snippets. (Action: Liam, due 2025-02-28)
- Design review with DevEx + SDK leads: review module boundaries and snippet id schema. (Invite list: Ravi, Sofia, Platform docs owners)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic and incremental. Aim for small wins (runnable quickstarts) first; API reference automation can be phased in.
- Please respond with concerns about backwards compatibility, sample-app location preferences, and any org constraints around localization budgets.
